mainEntity.name: How much does a Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI engine replacement costs between £2,800 and £5,500 supply-only for a rebuilt unit, with fitting adding £600-£1,200 depending on your location and whether you choose a Vauxhall specialist or main dealer. Used A20DT or A20DTH engines can be found from £1,000-£2,200, but come with no warranty and no upgraded components.

mainEntity.name: What are the common signs of engine failure in a Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI?

acceptedAnswer.text: For all Zafira 2.0 CDTI variants: engine management light illumination, loss of power, limp mode activation, rattling on cold start (timing chain wear), excessive smoke, and increased fuel consumption. For B20DTH models specifically: AdBlue warning lights and NOx sensor failures.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if your Zafira 2.0 CDTI is otherwise sound and has no major body or chassis issues. A 2014-2017 Zafira 2.0 CDTI values between £5,000 and £12,000, making a £2,800-£5,500 rebuilt engine replacement - around 25-45% of the car's value - a decision that depends on ownership horizon. For older examples under £4,000, evaluate scrap value before committing. For higher-value B20DTH examples over £8,000, replacement is usually justified.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI engine replacement typically takes 2-5 working days from delivery of the replacement engine. Specialist fitters often complete the work in 2-3 days, while main dealers may take 4-5 days due to scheduling. Mobile fitters offering supply & fit at your location may operate on different turnaround times.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI engine codes?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Zafira 2.0 CDTI range includes several engine codes with different power outputs. A20DT (110hp) and A20DTL (110hp) are entry-level Euro 5 units. A20DTH (160-165hp) is the higher-output Euro 5 variant. B20DTH (170hp, 400Nm) and D20DTH (170hp) are Euro 6 units with BlueInjection AdBlue technology from 2014 onwards.

mainEntity.name: Are Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI engines reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Zafira 2.0 CDTI is a generally robust and torquey diesel, but emissions system issues (EGR, DPF, AdBlue) are common on all modern diesels. The B20DTH is the most powerful and most complex, with additional BlueInjection SCR components that can fail. Timing chain wear is a known issue on higher-mileage examples. Regular servicing with the correct low-ash engine oil and motorway driving for DPF regeneration are essential for longevity.

historyTimeline.h2: Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI was introduced as a powerful and torquey diesel option across the Zafira B and Zafira C (Tourer) generations. The 2.0-litre diesel engine family evolved from the earlier Euro 5 A-series units (A20DT, A20DTH) to the more refined Euro 6 B-series engines (B20DTH, D20DTH) from 2014 onwards, bringing improved emissions, BlueInjection SCR technology, and increased torque.

milestones.description: Zafira B 2.0 CDTI introduced with 1.9 CDTI (Z19DTH) and later 2.0 CDTI (A20DT) variants
A20DTH introduced, 2.0-litre turbo diesel, 160-165hp, Euro 5 emissions
Zafira C (Tourer) launched with A20DT (110hp), A20DTH (165hp) and A20DTL (110hp) variants
B20DTH introduced, 2.0-litre turbo diesel, 170hp, 400Nm torque, Euro 6 with BlueInjection SCR
Zafira C production ends; 2.0 CDTI discontinued in Zafira range

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every 2.0 CDTI engine fitted to the Vauxhall Zafira is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI - particularly the A20DTH and B20DTH variants - is a punchy and torquey diesel that delivers strong performance. However, like all modern diesels, it suffers from emissions system failures (EGR, DPF, AdBlue) and age-related issues such as timing chain wear and injector failure. The B20DTH is the most powerful and generates the highest replacement demand. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Wear - "Why the Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI Timing Chain Wears Prematurely"
problems.rootCause: The timing chain and tensioner can wear, particularly on higher-output variants. Symptoms include rattling on cold start, engine management light illumination, and in severe cases, catastrophic engine failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New timing chain kit, tensioners, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Good preventative measure if caught early; 80,000-100,000 mile interval
When timing chain failure has caused valve or piston damage; often the most cost-effective route on higher-mileage examples

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2010-2015 Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI sits in the £3,000-£9,000 value band [THIRD-PARTY, Auto Trader 2025]. A timing chain replacement at £800-£1,500 is good value (15-25% of vehicle value). A full engine replacement at £2,800-£4,200 represents 30-50% of vehicle value - viable if the car is otherwise sound, but evaluate carefully on sub-£4,000 examples.
problems.recommendation: For the A20DTH and B20DTH, preventative timing chain inspection and replacement at 80,000-100,000 miles is strongly recommended. If the chain has already failed and caused internal damage, a rebuilt engine at £2,800-£4,200 offers better long-term reliability than attempting to repair a damaged bottom end.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B20DTH Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI engine prices

problems.h4: EGR/DPF/AdBlue System Failure - "Why the Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI Fails in Urban Driving"
problems.affectedModels: Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI (A20DT, A20DTH, A20DTL, B20DTH, D20DTH, 2008-2019)
problems.rootCause: Frequent short urban journeys prevent DPF regeneration cycles from completing, leading to soot buildup. EGR valves become clogged with carbon deposits. On Euro 6 B20DTH models, the BlueInjection AdBlue system can suffer from pump and NOx sensor failures.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical or manual DPF clean, EGR valve removal and carbon clearing
repairOptions.longevity: 20,000-30,000 mile fix; not a permanent solution if root driving habits persist

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: AdBlue pump, NOx sensor, or tank replacement
repairOptions.longevity: B20DTH models only; common from 60,000 miles
When emissions system failure has caused secondary turbo or injector damage; often best on higher-mileage examples

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2014-2019 Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI sits in the £5,000-£12,000 value band [THIRD-PARTY, Auto Trader 2025]. A full rebuild at £2,800-£5,500 represents 25-45% of vehicle value. For higher-value B20DTH examples (£8,000+), replacement is usually justified. For sub-£5,000 examples, evaluate carefully.
problems.recommendation: For Zafira 2.0 CDTI owners, regular motorway driving for DPF regeneration and using the correct low-ash engine oil are essential preventative measures. If EGR/DPF issues are caught early, a specialist clean at £300-£600 is good value. If the engine has gone into limp mode repeatedly and injectors or turbo show wear, a replacement rebuilt engine offers better long-term reliability than piecemeal repairs.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B20DTH Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI engine prices

problems.h4: Fuel Injector and Turbocharger Failure - "Why the Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI Loses Power and Misfires"
problems.rootCause: Injector failure (leak-off, electrical faults) and turbocharger wear (oil starvation, actuator failure, overboost) are common on higher-mileage examples. The overboost issue can trigger limp mode and the "service vehicle soon" warning.

repairOptions.longevity: Good if only 1-2 injectors failed; 30,000-50,000 mile fix

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Turbo rebuild or replacement, oil supply check
repairOptions.longevity: If turbo failure caught early; 40,000-60,000 mile fix
When multiple systems have failed; often best value on high-mileage examples

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2008-2014 Vauxhall Zafira 2.0 CDTI sits in the £2,500-£7,000 value band [THIRD-PARTY, Auto Trader 2025]. A full rebuild at £2,800-£4,500 represents 40-60% of vehicle value. For sub-£3,500 examples, evaluate scrap value before committing.
problems.recommendation: If injector or turbo failure occurs in isolation, repair is usually the right answer. If multiple systems have failed or the engine has high mileage (120,000+), a rebuilt engine with 12-month warranty offers better peace of mind than piecemeal repairs.
